candidates.name: IgG4-related hypophysitis
support_spans: A 56-year-old man presented with a 2-month history of bitemporal hemianopia and left labial numbness

Laboratory studies showed: TSH 0.658 μU/mL, free thyroxine 0.41 ng/dL, growth hormone 0.62 ng/mL, LH < 0.2 mIU/mL, FSH < 1.0 mIU/mL, prolactin 19.7 ng/mL, cortisol 0.5 μg/dL, ACTH 16.4 pg/mL, testosterone < 5.0 ng/dL, and IGF-1 119 ng/mL (−0.73 SD), consistent with hypopituitarism
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results are consistent with hypopituitarism, which is a common presentation of IgG4-related hypophysitis

candidates.name: Lymphocytic hypophysitis
support_spans: Pituitary MRI demonstrated diffuse swelling of the pituitary body and stalk, a 7-mm poorly enhancing mass in the right anterior lobe, loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot on T1-weighted images, and thickening of the sphenoid sinus mucosa
candidates.why: The patient's imaging findings are consistent with lymphocytic hypophysitis, which is a type of inflammation of the pituitary gland

candidates.name: IgG4-related disease
support_spans: Serum IgG4 was elevated at 319 mg/dL (normal 4.8–105), with a normal total IgG of 1284 mg/dL (IgG4/IgG ratio 0.25)
candidates.why: The patient's elevated IgG4 levels suggest an autoimmune mechanism, which is consistent with IgG4-related disease

key_evidence_spans: A 56-year-old man presented with a 2-month history of bitemporal hemianopia and left labial numbness

Laboratory studies showed: TSH 0.658 μU/mL, free thyroxine 0.41 ng/dL, growth hormone 0.62 ng/mL, LH < 0.2 mIU/mL, FSH < 1.0 mIU/mL, prolactin 19.7 ng/mL, cortisol 0.5 μg/dL, ACTH 16.4 pg/mL, testosterone < 5.0 ng/dL, and IGF-1 119 ng/mL (−0.73 SD), consistent with hypopituitarism

Pituitary MRI demonstrated diffuse swelling of the pituitary body and stalk, a 7-mm poorly enhancing mass in the right anterior lobe, loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot on T1-weighted images, and thickening of the sphenoid sinus mucosa
Serum IgG4 was elevated at 319 mg/dL (normal 4.8–105), with a normal total IgG of 1284 mg/dL (IgG4/IgG ratio 0.25)
Chest CT revealed a nodular lesion in the left lung field, raising suspicion for systemic IgG4-related disease
Dynamic pituitary stimulation tests confirmed gonadotropin, thyroid, and adrenal axis deficiencies and severe GH deficiency
